facts.text: Dixon was renamed around 1900 after Collins Dixon, a local resident, giving the town one of the few English-derived names in the region.
Al Hurricane, often called the 'Godfather' of New Mexico music, hails from Dixon.
The Embudo Valley’s microclimate, shaped by the Rio Grande and surrounding mountains, supports fruit orchards, vineyards, and nut trees.
Acequias, the first public works project of any land grant, began on September 20, 1725, and 10 historic acequias still hold senior water rights.
Since 1982, the Dixon Studio Tour—New Mexico’s longest-running arts event—draws visitors to over 40 studios, galleries, and farms each November.
Evidence shows the Embudo Valley was inhabited by Tiwa-speaking peoples linked to Picuris Pueblo over 6,000 years ago.
